claims.claim: The study used 652 Web of Science Core Collection papers from 2017–2023 and Bibliometrix, VOSviewer, and CiteSpace.
The search retrieved 843 candidates and manual title/abstract screening retained 652 records.
The corpus has 168 sources, 2,654 authors, and annual growth rate 149.8%.
Annual output was 1 in 2017 and 2018 and reached 243 in 2023.
China leads country output with 426 papers, followed by the United States with 142.
China and the United States hold leading positions and collaborate closely, while broader cooperation should improve.
The Chinese Academy of Sciences leads institutions with 39 papers, and the listed top institutions are Chinese.
Briefings in Bioinformatics leads journal output with 75 papers, while Bioinformatics has the highest total citations.
You Zhu-Hong, Deng Lei, and Zheng Mingyue are the three most productive authors.
The top-cited papers are Zitnik 2018, Altae-Tran 2017, and Xiong 2020.
Citation thresholds and TC/TP reflect research quality and impact.
China's lower average citations than the United States are caused by its later entry and shorter accumulation window.
Keywords show DTI, drug repurposing, and drug–drug interaction as main applications and graph convolutional methods as core algorithms.
Data availability, ethics, computing-resource balance, and interpretability are key technical challenges.
The field is at a high-growth stage with broad prospects and good development.
Corpus acquisition yielded 456 unique works via cursor pagination and exact deduplication.
Metadata coverage values across 11 fields are correctly reported.
The corpus spans 2018–2023; output rose from 1 to a peak of 190 and endpoint CAGR is 185.60%.
All records have the source-supplied article label, which cannot establish absence of review content.
Briefings in Bioinformatics, Thin Nguyen, and the Chinese Academy of Sciences lead source, author, and institution productivity.
Bradford Zone 1 has 5 sources and 148 documents, versus 120 sources and 151 documents in Zone 3.
Citation counts are right-skewed: mean 59.82, median 24, maximum 1,210, and 22 works uncited.
GraphDTA and Attentive FP are the two most-cited works and their abstracts report strong task results.
Computer science, artificial intelligence, and machine learning lead keyword frequency and rise over time.
The keyword network has 72 displayed nodes, 198 edges, and 7 clusters with a computer-science core.
The five reported social and intellectual network sizes and cluster counts match the outputs.
Growth and concentration establish a hot-topic, nascent phase.
Recency explains the uncited share.
Coupling and cocitation establish shared intellectual foundations.
Single-source, retrieval-date, citation-window, metadata, network-parameter, and productivity-quality limitations are explicit.

rationale: B provides the stronger evidence-bounded synthesis, with dense claim-to-evidence mapping and careful document-type, citation, network, and productivity caveats. A has valuable published-study detail but makes stronger quality, causal, and field-stage interpretations than its tabular and figure evidence establishes.

claims.claim: Corpus acquisition yielded 259 unique works via cursor pagination and exact deduplication.
The stated metadata completeness values are correct.
The corpus spans 2015–2022, rises from 2 to a peak of 72 works, has CAGR 66.85%, and declines only in 2021.
All records carry the source-supplied article label.
International Journal of Molecular Sciences leads sources, Xiaohui Chen leads authors, and Harvard, Peking, and Sun Yat-sen jointly lead institutions.
Bradford Zone 1 has 23 sources and 85 documents.
Citation mean is 72.09, median 32, maximum 1,436, and 35 works are uncited.
The most-cited record is a topically tangential 2022 Pseudomonas aeruginosa review.
The keyword network has 72 displayed nodes, 200 edges, and 5 clusters led by Biology, Gene, and Cell biology.
The coupling, coauthorship, institution, and cocitation network sizes and named leaders are correct.
The field is concentrated in high-impact journals.
Recent publication dates explain the uncited share.
Network maps establish strong intra-institutional and intra-national collaboration.
The journals and institutions establish a trans-Pacific leadership axis.
Single-source, metadata, citation-window, source-classification, CAGR, productivity, and network limitations are explicit.
The study used 219 WoSCC records on CRISPR-related extracellular-vesicle research from 2015–2022.
The final corpus followed screening from 231 records and contains 164 articles and 55 reviews.
R, VOSviewer, CiteSpace, and GraphPad Prism were used for bibliometric and keyword analyses.
Annual output rose over the period and the relative research-interest metric was analyzed.
China leads publication count; the United States leads total citations and H-index; Canada leads average citations.
Wang Y. and Zhang H. each published six papers, while Zhao X.X. has the highest average citations among the top six.
The analysis identifies 141 core authors and 31 countries for collaboration mapping.
The USA, England, Germany, China, and Canada lead country collaboration link strength.
The collaboration maps establish a domestic-partner preference and geographic restriction.
Nature, PNAS, and Nature Communications are the three most cocited journals.
The reference cocitation map has three clusters covering CRISPR/Cas, EV delivery, and EV-characterization reviews.
The keyword analysis uses 317 keywords occurring at least twice and identifies seven clusters.
Expression, cells, Cas9, RNA, CRISPR/Cas9, cancer, and exosome are leading keywords.
The literature evolved from mechanism and target studies in 2015–2020 toward delivery, gene therapy, nanomaterials, and translation in 2020–2022.
Citation bursts directly measure author or journal popularity and research quality.

rationale: A is more reproducible and cautious while covering the main performance and network results. B is richly descriptive but overinterprets citation bursts and collaboration maps as quality, popularity, geographic restriction, and domestic preference, with fewer limitations on database and citation-window effects.
